proposals.relationship: Uses White’s account of critical history to frame an ethically responsible relation between historical inquiry and educational change (1976).
proposals.evidence_note: Own382/n1 cites The Burden of History. A specific methodological resource, not endorsement of White’s entire narrative theory or a claim of personal formation. Original essay unread.

proposals.relationship: Draws on Dobb’s definition of capitalism through commodified labour power to distinguish capitalist from industrial change (1976).
proposals.evidence_note: Own391/n20. Katz treats the three-stage model as partly speculative. Marx’s Capital is also cited in the note, but the explicit definition is assigned to Dobb; the original books remain unread.

proposals.relationship: Uses Thompson’s analysis of work discipline to connect the habits demanded by industrial work with school-system formation (1976).
proposals.evidence_note: Own395/n27 names Thompson’s account; Gutman’s Work,Culture and Society is a second cited resource in the same note. No exclusive lineage or full reading of either original essay.

proposals.relationship: Applies Davis’s distinction between ideology’s social functions and conscious intentions to popular acceptance of public schooling (1976).
proposals.evidence_note: Own400/n38–39 uses Davis’s antislavery analysis for the problem of consent. This is an analytical transfer, not a claim that schools and slavery are identical; Katz rejects equating imposition with conspiracy. Davis’s1975book remains unread.

proposals.relationship: Uses Gramsci’s distinction between coercion and consent, explicitly through Davis, to analyze the acceptance of public education (1976).
proposals.evidence_note: Own400/n36 expressly identifies Gramsci as quoted in Davis’s1975bookp349. The mediated route is preserved; Gramsci’s original work and Davis’s book remain unread. Distinct from Davis’s own explanation of ideological functions.

proposals.relationship: Uses Scott and Louise Tilly’s joint work among the resources for explaining women’s occupational alternatives and the feminization of teaching (1976).
proposals.evidence_note: Own389/n18 cites their joint Women’s Work and the Family alongside PatriciaBranca,TheresaMcBride and Katz’s own work. This identifies a bounded contextual resource, not sole authorship or a general Scott influence; LouiseTilly lacks a full endpoint. Cited original essay unread.

proposals.relationship: Sugrue recalls Katz’s intellectual inspiration, sustained guidance and support from the period of his dissertation onward.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2014memorial reproduced by PennPress: Sugrue describes the poverty-history group, ongoing support and the effect of reading The Undeserving Poor. Not inferred from coediting, appointment or formal supervision; neither the memorial’s1988book date nor the1998collection is assigned as a verified first-publication or causal starting date.
primary_locators: Sugrue memorial25August2014, first-meeting paragraph and Undeserving Poor recollection

proposals.relationship: Makes Du Bois’s research methods and agenda a framework for examining race and the American welfare state (2000).
proposals.evidence_note: Authorial abstract expressly states the analytical use. Scope is this article’s declared framework; full body and DuBois originals unread. Does not infer intellectual transmission merely from the1998edited collection’s title.

proposals.relationship: Describes population reconstruction from linked census and assessment records as a way to examine social structure and family organization (1976).
proposals.evidence_note: Own382–383 explains Hamilton research and collaborative extension to Buffalo/ErieCounty. A particular research practice, not sole credit for shared data or a foundation claim. Existing urban and social-history relationships remain distinct.

proposals.relationship: Investigates family organization, youth semi-autonomy and household change through the Hamilton research, qualifying the proposed historical pattern (1976).
proposals.evidence_note: Own386–388 explicitly calls the semi-autonomy account tenuous and partly speculative. Stern’s2017retrospective769credits Katz,Doucet and Stern’s collaborative family-economy work and the constraints on family strategy. Contribution to a specific research problem, not a settled universal model; original books unread.
